title: The Serf Who Wrote a Nation: Moryntsi, the Aral Steppe, and the Hill Above the Dnieper
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Moryntsi, the birth in bondage
stops.date_confidence: attested; New Style, 25 February Old Style in the same sources
stops.campa: A son is born in Moryntsi, in Zvenyhorodka county of the Kyiv gubernia, to Hryhorii and Kateryna Shevchenko, who belong, with the village and its fields, to the landowner Vasily Engelhardt. The child is property before he is a person, and his name enters the estate rolls the way a head of livestock enters them. Ukraine at this date has no state of its own, no press in its own tongue, and no literature the empire is willing to call a literature. The boy will supply the third of these, and the other two will one day be built on it.
suggested_refs: The Engelhardt estate rolls of Moryntsi, Zvenyhorodka county

stops.name: Kyrylivka, the two graves
stops.date_confidence: attested; the family's move to Kyrylivka dated 1816, the mother's death 1 September 1823
stops.campa: The family has moved to Kyrylivka, southwest of the village where he was born. His mother Kateryna dies in September 1823. His father Hryhorii dies in April 1825, and the boy is orphaned at eleven, still the property of the estate that owns the graves. The father's testament, as the household remembers it, leaves the boy nothing, because the boy will either come to nothing or become something no inheritance can help. Kyrylivka will be renamed Shevchenkove within a century, after the child buried nobody and was owned by everybody.
suggested_refs: The churchyard of Kyrylivka, now Shevchenkove, Zvenyhorodka raion

stops.name: Lysianka, the deacon's boy
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month from the English timeline; the runaway episode itself is tradition rather than document
stops.campa: Hired out to a deacon at Lysianka, he learns letters and psalter and takes beatings for both. The placement fails, as the placements before it failed. He runs, aged about thirteen, along roads he does not own and cannot legally travel, and is brought back. What the deacon's house gives him is the only formal schooling of his life: the Slavonic psalms, learned by rote under a stick, which will surface forty years later in the cadence of poems the Russian censor reads aloud in evidence against him.
suggested_refs: The deacon's school at Lysianka, one of several failed placements of the orphan years

stops.name: Tarasivka, the first paint
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the site, the outcome and the coordinate are all approximate and appear in no primary source reached
stops.campa: Tradition sends him here to work under village icon painters, grinding pigment and filling in gold, before the estate reclaims him. No document confirms it and the coordinate is a guess within a few kilometres. What the tradition insists on is the order of events: he handles paint before he handles a pen, and for the rest of his life the two occupations run in harness. The empire will eventually forbid him both in the same sentence, which is a kind of confirmation that the tradition understood him.
suggested_refs: Village icon workshops of the Zvenyhorodka district in the 1820s
sources: Traditional biographical accounts; flagged [R] in the research report

stops.name: Vilnius, the serf in a painter's city
stops.date_confidence: the Vilnius years attested 1828-31 by Encyclopedia of Ukraine and from autumn 1829 by Ukrainian Wikipedia; the named teacher is disputed
stops.campa: Pavel Engelhardt, heir to the estate, takes the boy into household service as a houseboy and carries him to Vilnius. Here he sees academic painting for the first time and draws on whatever he can reach. Who taught him is contested: the English record names Franciszek Ksawery Lampi, who worked in Warsaw and not here, while the literature usually names Jan Rustem of the Vilnius school, and the Encyclopedia of Ukraine names nobody at all. A serf's instruction leaves no enrollment book. He is punished for drawing at night and keeps drawing at night.
suggested_refs: The Vilnius drawing school of Jan Rustem, the milieu the serf attendant moved through

stops.name: Warsaw, the contested apprenticeship
stops.date_confidence: contested; asserted only by the English Wikipedia timeline, denied by implication by Encyclopedia of Ukraine and Ukrainian Wikipedia, which keep him in Vilnius throughout; if it happened it belongs to 1830-31
stops.campa: One source in three sends the household west to Warsaw and apprentices him to a painter-decorator there. The other two keep him in Vilnius without a break until the winter of 1831. The stop is carried here on one authority against two, marked as what it is, because a serf's movements are recorded only when his owner's convenience requires recording them. Whether or not he stood in Warsaw, the Polish rising of November 1830 is what moves the household next, and it moves it east.
suggested_refs: The Warsaw episode of the English biographical timeline, unconfirmed elsewhere
sources: Contradicted by Encyclopedia of Ukraine and Ukrainian Wikipedia; see report

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, apprenticed to Shiriaev
stops.date_confidence: attested for the four-year apprenticeship; the household reaches the capital in early 1831, not 1830 as some timelines have it
stops.campa: The November Uprising empties Vilnius of Engelhardt's household and the capital receives it. Engelhardt contracts his serf out for about four years to the decorative painter Vasilii Shiriaev, who sets him to ceilings, theatre scenery and palace ornament. On white nights he goes to the Summer Garden and copies the statues by the light that never quite fails, and there Karl Briullov, the most famous painter in the empire, is shown the drawings of a man who cannot legally own the paper. Alexander von Humboldt had passed through this same capital on the Tsar's commission a year before he arrived.
suggested_refs: Vasilii Shiriaev's decorative painting workshop, Saint Petersburg

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, bought out of serfdom for 2,500 rubles
stops.date_confidence: attested by Encyclopedia of Ukraine and English Wikipedia; the pool's earlier [R] tag on this transaction was wrong and is raised to attested
stops.campa: Briullov paints a portrait of the poet Vasily Zhukovsky. The portrait is raffled among the imperial family. The lottery raises 2,500 rubles, and with that sum a man is bought from another man and handed to himself. He is twenty-four. Nine years later the chief of the gendarmes will cite this very transaction against him in a courtroom, arguing that a serf freed by the money of the August Family owed the August Family gratitude rather than verse. He dedicates the poem Katerina to Zhukovsky, in memory of April 22, 1838.
suggested_refs: Karl Briullov's portrait of Vasily Zhukovsky, raffled to purchase Shevchenko's manumission

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Academy under Briullov
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month inferred; the silver medal follows in April 1839, typhus in November 1839
stops.campa: He enters the Imperial Academy of Arts as a student under Briullov's supervision, a freedman of six months among the sons of officials. In April of the following year the Academy gives him a silver medal. In November typhus nearly finishes him. He is drawing well enough to live by it, and he is beginning to write in a language that has no publisher, no readership organized as a readership, and no standing in the eyes of the ministry that licenses print. He writes in it anyway, and the writing is not a hobby beside the painting.
suggested_refs: The Imperial Academy of Arts on Vasilievsky Island, his school, his lodging, and the place of his death

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Kobzar of eight poems
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month unknown; the print run of 1,000 by E. F. Fischer is attested, the claim that the censor destroyed material from the first hundred copies is not corroborated
stops.campa: A thin book appears in the imperial capital with eight Romantic poems in Ukrainian and the title Kobzar, the word for a blind itinerant singer of the steppe who carries the past in a bandura and a memory. One thousand copies from the press of E. F. Fischer. It is the moment a peasant vernacular that the empire calls Little Russian, a dialect, a joke of the servants' hall, becomes a literature with an author's name on the spine. Everything Ukrainian that follows in print for a hundred years dates itself from this book.
stops.quote: Have your love, you black haired maidens, / But avoid the Moskals, / For the Moskals--they are strangers, / And they treat you foully.
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko, "Katerina," translated by Clarence A. Manning, in Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 3741-3744
suggested_refs: The 1840 Kobzar, Saint Petersburg, printed by E. F. Fischer in 1,000 copies

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, Haidamaky
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month unknown
stops.campa: The epic Haidamaky is published: the peasant risings of the eighteenth century told from the inside, with the knives and the churches burning and no narrator standing at a safe distance to apologize for it. Censors let it through in a mutilated state. Readers in Kyiv and Poltava copy out by hand what the censors cut. Three years later a fuller Chyhyryn Kobzar will gather the poem into the collection, and the collection will begin to travel the empire in the luggage of students who understand exactly what it is they are carrying.
suggested_refs: Haidamaky, 1841, and its incorporation into the Chyhyryn Kobzar of 1844

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, The Dream is written
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month unknown; Hamaliia and the etching album Picturesque Ukraine belong to the same year
stops.campa: In one year he publishes the ballad Hamaliia, issues the etching album Zhivopisnaia Ukraina, and writes Son, The Dream: a satire that walks the reader through the imperial court and holds the tsar and the tsaritsa up for inspection like specimens. He does not print it. He reads it aloud to friends and lets copies pass from hand to hand, which in an autocracy is publication. Three years from now those copies will be pulled out of other men's papers and laid on a desk in front of Nicholas the First.
suggested_refs: Zhivopisnaia Ukraina (Picturesque Ukraine), the 1844 album of etchings
Son (The Dream), 1844, circulated in manuscript

stops.name: Kyiv, the first return as a free man
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1843, day unknown
stops.campa: Fourteen years after a landlord's cart took him north, he comes back over the same border as a graduate of the Academy with money in his pocket and a book with his name on it. He sketches the churches and the earthworks of the old capital. He meets young men who will shortly form a secret brotherhood, and they meet a man whose poems they already know by heart. The country he returns to is the country he has been writing, and the fit between the two is close enough to frighten the people who read him.
suggested_refs: Shevchenko's 1843 Kyiv sketches of monuments and earthworks

stops.name: Yahotyn, the Repnin house
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month inferred from the itinerary of the 1843 visit
stops.campa: The household of Prince Nikolai Repnin takes him in as a guest and a portraitist, and the prince's daughter Varvara forms an attachment to him that neither his birth nor his temperament allows to go anywhere. She writes to him for the rest of his life, including through the ten years when writing to him is imprudent and reaching him is difficult. Fifteen years from now he will meet her again in Moscow on his road back from the Caspian, and will note in his diary, with the coolness of a man who has been told nothing, that she seems improved.
suggested_refs: The Repnin estate at Yahotyn and the Repnina correspondence

stops.name: Kyrylivka, the siblings after fourteen years
stops.date_confidence: autumn 1843 attested, month approximate
stops.campa: He walks back into the village of the two graves and finds his brothers and his sister alive and still owned, bound to the heirs of the man who sold him to himself. He is the only free Shevchenko in Kyrylivka. He eats at their table as a gentleman from the capital and leaves as one, and this arithmetic, one purchased freedom against a family and a nation still in bondage, is what turns a Romantic poet of the steppe into a political problem. He will spend the rest of his working life trying to buy the rest of them out.
suggested_refs: The surviving Shevchenko siblings of Kyrylivka, serfs of the Engelhardt heirs

stops.name: Kyiv, the Archeographic Commission
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month inferred; he graduates from the Academy the same year
stops.campa: He graduates from the Academy and takes a post with the Kyiv Archeographic Commission, which pays him to travel Russian-ruled Ukraine drawing ruins, tombs and churches and writing down what the peasants sing. The empire is funding an inventory of its province. He is compiling the evidence file of a nation. The same portfolio serves both purposes without alteration, which is why the work is possible at all, and why, when the arrests come, the drawings will be read as innocent and the poems as treason.
suggested_refs: The Kyiv Archeographic Commission survey portfolios, 1845-1846

stops.name: Pereiaslav, the Testament written
stops.date_confidence: date and poem attested; the Pereiaslav location is scholarly consensus, not confirmed against a primary document here
stops.campa: Ill in a house at Pereiaslav on Christmas Day, he writes fourteen lines of instruction for his own burial: a grave on a hill above the Dnieper, in Ukraine, where he can hear the river move. It is a poem and it is a will, and both halves of it will be executed. Sixteen years from now his coffin will come up that river under sail and the hill will be found and the ground opened, and the poem will be set to music twice and sung by people who will not be able to say who wrote it.
stops.quote: When I die, O lay my body / In a lofty tomb / Out upon the steppes unbounded / In my own dear Ukraine.
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko, "The Testament" (Zapovit), written 25 December 1845, translated by Clarence A. Manning, Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 7420-7423
suggested_refs: Zapovit (The Testament), 25 December 1845, Pereiaslav

stops.name: Kyiv, the Brotherhood denounced
stops.date_confidence: 5 April 1847 for his own arrest; the same source dates the round-up of the society to March 1847, a discrepancy left standing
stops.campa: The Brotherhood of Saints Cyril and Methodius wants a federation of free Slavic peoples and the end of serfdom, meets in Kyiv, and numbers perhaps a dozen men. A student informs. The police take the members and their papers, and among the papers is Son, The Dream. Shevchenko is arrested on the road to a wedding. At the interrogation he admits having written insolent and satirical works, and gives the reason in the language of the psalter he learned at Lysianka under a stick.
stops.quote: forgetting his conscience and the fear of God
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko's own statement at his interrogation, 1847, quoted in Clarence A. Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, line 1104
suggested_refs: The 1847 case file of the Brotherhood of Saints Cyril and Methodius, Third Section

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Peter and Paul Fortress
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day inferred; the fortress detention itself is carried by one source and tagged as reconstruction in the report
stops.campa: He is brought north to the fortress on the Neva and held while the case is decided. The Academy is asked what kind of man it educated. Its president answers in a register the gendarmes were not asking for, praising the poems and the man who wrote them, and the testimony is entered into the file of a treason inquiry as if literary merit were an argument in law. It is not. But it is preserved, and it is the only voice in the record that speaks of him as a poet rather than as a defendant.
stops.quote: It is necessary to add that Shevchenko has a gift for poetry and in the Little Russian language has written several poems, respected by people who are familiar with the Little Russian language and the former life of this region; he was always considered as a moral man, perhaps something of a dreamer and an honorer of the Little Russian past, but nothing prejudicial came to the knowledge of the Academy.
stops.quote_source: Count Lakhtenberg, President of the Academy of Arts, testimony at the 1847 inquiry, quoted in Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 1093-1100
suggested_refs: The Peter and Paul Fortress prison, Saint Petersburg, holding place during the 1847 inquiry

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the tsar's hand on the sentence
stops.date_confidence: the sentence of 26 May 1847 is attested in translation; that Nicholas I wrote the additional clause in his own hand is universal tradition, carried as reconstruction
stops.campa: Count Orlov, chief of the gendarmes, sums the evidence: a serf freed by the money of the August Family, who answered with verses of the most revolting character. The sentence sends him to the Orenburg Special Corps as a private soldier, healthy constitution noted, with the right to earn his freedom by honorable service. Then a second hand adds a clause the law did not require and no court had asked for. Alexander von Humboldt had crossed the Urals eighteen years earlier on a commission from the same sovereign.
stops.quote: Under the strictest supervision with a prohibition of writing and sketching.
stops.quote_source: Tsar Nicholas I, handwritten addition to Shevchenko's sentence, 1847, quoted in Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 1142-1144
suggested_refs: The sentence of 26 May 1847 with the imperial addition
sources: Atlas journey: humboldt (Urals and Siberian steppe, 1829-09)

stops.name: Orsk fortress, the private soldier
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day unknown
stops.campa: Two thousand kilometres from the Academy, on the bare frontier of the Orenburg steppe, the poet of Ukraine is issued a uniform and taught the drill. He is thirty-three. The garrison is a square of earth walls with nothing outside it in any direction, and the sentence has no end date attached. Officers are instructed to watch him. He is forbidden to write and forbidden to draw, which is to say he is forbidden the two activities that constitute him, and the prohibition is the point of the punishment rather than an incident of it.
suggested_refs: Orsk fortress on the Ural river, garrison of the Orenburg Special Corps

stops.name: Raim on the Syr Darya, the expedition assembles
stops.date_confidence: May 1848 attested; the coordinate is approximate, the fort site is eroded and no gazetteer entry for Raim itself was found
stops.campa: Lieutenant Aleksei Butakov needs a draughtsman for the first survey of the Aral Sea and finds one in the ranks. Against the letter of the sentence, the private is attached to the expedition and put to work with pencil and brush for the scientific record of the imperial navy. The march to the post crosses the Karakum on foot. The empire that has forbidden him to draw now requires him to draw, and neither Butakov nor Shevchenko sees any reason to raise the contradiction with Saint Petersburg.
suggested_refs: The Raim (Raiym) post near the Syr Darya delta, staging point of Butakov's 1848 Aral survey

stops.name: The Aral Sea, aboard the schooner Konstantin
stops.date_confidence: the 1848 and 1849 sailing seasons are attested; the month and the mid-sea coordinate are nominal
stops.campa: The schooner is carried in pieces across the steppe and assembled on the shore, and for two seasons it sails a sea no chart has yet described. Shevchenko draws the coasts, the water, the low sandbanks and the men. These sheets are the reason the expedition has a visual record and they are also, in law, evidence of a crime committed daily under a commanding officer's protection. Eleven years later he will meet Butakov again in a Russian provincial town and write down what the memory of this water does to him.
stops.quote: My heart grows cold at the very memory of that wilderness, but I think he is ready to settle down there forever.
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko, Journal, entry of 10 March 1858, on meeting Captain Butakov, quoted in Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 1409-1412
suggested_refs: The Aral survey drawings of 1848-1849, made in defiance of the imperial ban

stops.name: Kos-Aral, the wintering
stops.date_confidence: the expedition winters here over 1848-49, not in 1849 as the working pool had it
stops.campa: The expedition puts in on the island station and waits out the ice. Here, where there is nothing to do and nobody to report him, he writes the Kos-Aral cycle, some of the strongest lyric poetry of his life, on paper he is not supposed to have, in a language the garrison cannot read. Genghis Khan's armies crossed this same corridor of steppe six centuries before on their way to Urgench. The empire has calculated that a man can be silenced by being sent where nobody speaks his language. The calculation is exactly backwards.
suggested_refs: The Kos-Aral poems, written during the winter of 1848-1849

stops.name: Orenburg, the drawings confiscated
stops.date_confidence: he returns from the Aral in late 1849; the denunciation, arrest and confiscation are dated April 1850
stops.campa: Back in the provincial capital he lives almost like a man, visits friends, wears civilian clothes. Someone reports him. The drawings from the Aral, made at a naval officer's request for the empire's own charts, are seized as proof that the prisoner has been drawing. He is arrested for the coat on his back and for the pencil in his hand. The punishment is transfer, and the place chosen for the transfer is selected on one criterion, which is that no friend and no post road reaches it easily.
suggested_refs: The April 1850 denunciation at Orenburg and the seizure of the Aral portfolio

stops.name: Novopetrovske fortification, the seven years
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1850; he remains until August 1857
stops.campa: A fortification on the Caspian shore of the Mangyshlak peninsula, on a spit of rock with a garrison and a well and the sea on three sides. He arrives in October 1850 and is still here in the summer of 1857. This is the hardest stretch: no expedition to attach himself to, no officer minded to bend the order, close supervision and the standing ban. He is a soldier in his late thirties drilling with recruits half his age. The place is called Fort-Shevchenko today, which is the empire's sentence read back to it in reverse.
suggested_refs: Novopetrovske fortification, Mangyshlak, renamed Fort-Shevchenko

stops.name: Novopetrovske, the booklets in the boot
stops.date_confidence: tradition; the notebooks survive, the detail of their concealment is universal in the biographies and not independently documented here, and the year is nominal within 1850-1857
stops.campa: He sews small notebooks by hand, writes verse into them in a script cramped to save paper, and hides them in his boots when the officers walk through. The books exist; where exactly he kept them is what the tradition supplies. Every line written in that fortification is a punishable act committed against a sovereign's personal instruction, and he commits it for seven years without a break. A Canadian translator will state the fact plainly in 1922, in a sentence that carries no rhetoric because it does not need any.
stops.quote: They forbade him to write but he wrote verses secretly and concealed them.
stops.quote_source: Biographical note in Alexander Jardine Hunter (trans.), The Kobzar of the Ukraine (Canada, 1922), Project Gutenberg #68486, lines 2946-2947
suggested_refs: The hand-sewn Novopetrovske notebooks, the so-called bootleg booklets
sources: Standard Shevchenko biographical tradition; flagged [R] in the report

stops.name: Novopetrovske, the word Liberty
stops.date_confidence: attested by his own journal entry of that date
stops.campa: Nicholas the First has been dead two years and the amnesty has finally reached the Caspian. On the morning of 21 July 1857 a mail boat comes in. Shevchenko shaves, walks back from the fort, and is met on the road by the man in charge of the post hospital, who does not begin with a greeting. He records the hour. He is forty-three years old and has been a soldier for ten of them. He writes the moment down in his journal the way a navigator writes a position, because it is one.
stops.quote: and from the non-commissioned officer Kulikh I first learned that at nine o'clock in the morning a mail boat had arrived. Having shaved, and with sinking heart, I returned to the city and, leaving the fort, I met Bazhanov who was in charge of the post hospital. And he first greeted me with Liberty: July 21, 1857, at eleven o'clock in the morning.
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko, Journal, entry of 21 July 1857, Novopetrovsk fortress, quoted in Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 1313-1319
suggested_refs: Shevchenko's Journal, begun at Novopetrovske and kept through the return

stops.name: Astrakhan, the Volga road north
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction of the return route; the Caspian and Volga passage is standard but the Astrakhan stop is not separately documented here
stops.campa: He crosses the Caspian and enters the Volga at its mouth. From here the river carries him north through the whole length of the empire that sentenced him, past Sarai where the Golden Horde kept its capital and Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta both stopped, past Saratov where the child Helena Blavatsky was living sixteen years before. He is not going to Ukraine. He is going to whatever provincial town the ministry names, because a released prisoner is still an assigned man.
suggested_refs: The 1857 Caspian and Volga return passage
sources: Standard reconstruction of the 1857 route; flagged [R] in the report
Atlas journeys: marco_polo and ibn_battuta (Sarai), blavatsky (Saratov, 1841)

stops.name: Nizhny Novgorod, held short of the capital
stops.date_confidence: attested; he is held here from September 1857 into March 1858
stops.campa: Freed and forbidden: he may not live in Saint Petersburg, he may not live in Moscow, and Ukraine is closed to him. He is set down in Nizhny Novgorod and told to wait. He resumes his journal, writes letters to everyone in the capital who owes him a favour or admires his work, and draws portraits for money. The amnesty has released him from the army and into a smaller cage. He is forty-three, he has published nothing in seventeen years, and the reading public of two empires believes he is dead.
suggested_refs: The Nizhny Novgorod months and the resumed Journal, 1857-1858

stops.name: Nizhny Novgorod, the news on his birthday
stops.date_confidence: attested as the date he receives the news here, Old Style, his birthday; the working pool wrongly read this as the date of his arrival in the capital
stops.campa: On 25 February 1858, his forty-fourth birthday by the old calendar, word arrives in Nizhny Novgorod that permission has been granted and he may go to Saint Petersburg. He does not leave at once. Two weeks later Captain Butakov of the Aral survey passes through, and the two men who charted a sea together under an illegal arrangement sit down as free men, and the poet finds that the wilderness is still cold in him and that his old commander misses it.
suggested_refs: The permission of February 1858, received at Nizhny Novgorod

stops.name: Moscow, Repnina and Shchepkin
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 1858, day unknown
stops.campa: On the road north he stops in Moscow. Varvara Repnina, who has written to him across ten years of exile, is here, and so is Mikhail Shchepkin, the greatest actor in Russia and, like Shevchenko, a man born owned and bought out of it. The two former serfs embrace in a city where that fact is a curiosity rather than a scandal. Of Repnina, whom he has not seen in fifteen years and who has spent them thinking about him, he records an observation of remarkable obtuseness.
stops.quote: She has changed for the better; she looks as if she had grown younger, and were rushing into matrimony, a thing which I had not noticed previously. Has she not met in Moscow a good confessor?
stops.quote_source: Shevchenko, diary entry of 17 March 1858, on Princess Repnina, quoted in Manning, Taras Shevchenko (1945), Project Gutenberg #78316, lines 1418-1421
suggested_refs: The Moscow reunion with Varvara Repnina and Mikhail Shchepkin, March 1858

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Academy gives him rooms
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1858; he reaches the capital in late March 1858
stops.campa: The institution that trained him and the empire that sentenced him are the same state, and it now installs him in a workshop and lodgings within the Academy walls. Literary Petersburg receives him as a returned celebrity, Russian and Ukrainian at once. He takes up etching seriously and will be named an academician for it. He is a decade older than his body's account of him, he drinks, and the men who see him at parties describe a face that has been out on the steppe and has brought some of it back.
suggested_refs: Shevchenko's workshop and lodgings at the Imperial Academy of Arts, 1858-1861

stops.name: Kyiv, the last passage through
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1859
stops.campa: Permission to enter Ukraine is granted at last and he crosses in June 1859, thirteen years after the arrest. He passes through Kyiv, sees the friends who are not in exile or dead, and goes on south into the country of his birth. He is looking for land. The plan is a house above the Dnieper, a wife, and the rest of a working life spent on the right side of a border he has crossed under guard twice. He has twenty months to live and does not know it, and neither does anybody watching him.
suggested_refs: The 1859 travel permission and the last Ukrainian journey

stops.name: Kyrylivka, the brother and the sister still bound
stops.date_confidence: 1859 attested, month and day approximate within the summer itinerary
stops.campa: The last visit to the village. His brother Mykyta and his sister Iryna are alive and still serfs, sixteen years after he stood in this house as the only free member of the family and twenty-one years after the lottery that freed him. Emancipation is two years away and neither of them knows it. He has spent his adult life writing about serfdom for readers who consider it a subject; here it is a kitchen, a sister, and a bill of sale still in force.
suggested_refs: Mykyta and Iryna Shevchenko of Kyrylivka, serfs until 1861

stops.name: Prokhorivka, Mykhailova Hora above the river
stops.date_confidence: the visit is attested; the coordinate is corrected to the left bank at Prokhorivka, opposite Kaniv, and is approximate
stops.campa: He climbs to the estate of the scholar Mykhailo Maksymovych, first rector of Kyiv University and collector of Ukrainian folk song, on the high left bank opposite Kaniv. From the terrace the Dnieper runs south past the hills he has been describing in verse since 1845. He walks the ground nearby with his brother-in-law Varfolomii, pricing plots, planning a house. He is standing within sight of the hill where he will be buried in twenty-two months, looking at it as real estate.
suggested_refs: Mykhailo Maksymovych's Mykhailova Hora estate at Prokhorivka

stops.name: Cherkasy district, arrested for blasphemy
stops.date_confidence: July 1859 attested, day unknown; the arrest is in the Cherkasy district, not at Priorka in Kyiv as the working pool had it
stops.campa: Someone downriver reports him to the local police for blasphemy. He is arrested and transported to Kyiv via Cherkasy, interrogated, and released. Nobody in the administration believes the charge and nobody needs to: the file records that the man who was sentenced in 1847 is still travelling, still talking, still watched, and the point of the exercise is the record. Released, he takes lodging in Priorka on the northern edge of Kyiv, and is ordered back to Saint Petersburg. He never sees Ukraine again.
suggested_refs: The July 1859 blasphemy denunciation and the Priorka lodging in Kyiv

stops.name: Kachanivka, the Tarnovsky house
stops.date_confidence: 1859 attested, month approximate; coordinate corrected to the palace itself
stops.campa: On the road north he stops at the Tarnovsky estate, a park and a palace where the Ukrainian writers and painters of the century come to argue and be fed. He plays the piano badly, sings, and leaves. The family that receives him here will pay, twenty-five years from now, for the cast-iron cross over his grave and for the first museum of the Kobzar built beside it. This is the last Ukrainian roof he sleeps under. He recrosses the border into the empire's interior in the ordinary way, as a passenger.
suggested_refs: Kachanivka Palace and the Tarnovsky collection of Shevchenko material

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the primer and the dropsy
stops.date_confidence: the Bukvar is published in 1860; the dropsy diagnosis is attested to December 1860
stops.campa: Failing, he spends the last well months of his life on a schoolbook. The Bukvar Iuzhnorusskii is a Ukrainian primer, cheap, meant to teach peasants to read in their own language, and he pays for it himself and gives copies away. It is the least literary thing he ever produced and the most direct: a nation is people who can read each other. In December the doctors name dropsy, edema from a heart and liver worn out by ten years of garrison rations and the drinking that followed them.
suggested_refs: Bukvar Iuzhnorusskii, the 1860 Ukrainian primer, printed at the author's expense

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the last poem
stops.date_confidence: attested, Old Style, twelve days before his death by the same calendar
stops.campa: He writes his last poem twelve days before he dies, in a room in the Academy, swollen and short of breath. The engagement to Lykera Polusmakova, a young former serf, has broken down. The house above the Dnieper was never bought. Emancipation is signed in this same month across the empire and he lives just long enough for the news of it to be in the air of the capital, though not long enough to see what it does or fails to do in the village where his brother and sister are still counted as property.
suggested_refs: The final poem of February 1861

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, death in the Academy workshop
stops.date_confidence: attested; New Style, 26 February Old Style, the day after his birthday by that calendar
stops.campa: He dies in his workshop at the Imperial Academy of Arts, forty-seven years old, of dropsy. Dostoevsky, Turgenev, Saltykov-Shchedrin and Leskov come to the funeral. The empire buries a Russian academician and a Ukrainian poet in the same coffin and has never entirely agreed since on which of the two it was. He was born owned by a man and dies owned by a literature. The room he dies in is inside the institution that both trained him and, at the other end of the same corridor of state, sentenced him.
suggested_refs: The Academy workshop where Shevchenko died, 1861

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, the Smolensk Cemetery
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day inferred; a temporary burial of some ten weeks
stops.campa: He is put in the ground on Vasilievsky Island, in the capital that bought him, freed him, tried him, exiled him, released him and housed him. His friends begin at once to organize what the poem requires. Permission to move a political convict's body across the empire to a hill in Ukraine is not a small administrative matter, and it is granted. The grave here is open for ten weeks and then emptied, and Smolensk Cemetery keeps a marker for a man who is not in it.
suggested_refs: The temporary grave at the Smolensk Cemetery, Saint Petersburg, March to May 1861

stops.name: Kaniv, Chernecha Hora: the hill in the poem
stops.date_confidence: attested; New Style, 8 May Old Style
stops.campa: The coffin comes up the Dnieper by boat and is carried to the top of Monks' Hill above Kaniv, and the instruction written in a sickroom at Pereiaslav in 1845 is carried out to the letter. The people of the district rename the height Tarasova Hora. A wooden cross marks it; Vasyl Tarnovsky the Younger pays for a cast-iron one in 1884, with the first folk museum of the Kobzar beside it, and Soviet authority takes the cross down in the 1920s and the hillside becomes a state reserve in 1925.
stops.quote: After being set to music by H. Hladky in the 1870s, the poem achieved a status second only to Ukraine's national anthem.
stops.quote_source: Encyclopedia of Ukraine, entry 'Shevchenko, Taras,' on Zapovit; Ukrainian Wikipedia dates the rival Lysenko and Hladky melodies to 1868, a discrepancy left standing
suggested_refs: Chernecha Hora, Taras Hill, and the Taras Shevchenko National Reserve at Kaniv

stops.name: Washington, the memorial on P Street
stops.date_confidence: attested; Eisenhower unveiled the statue as a former president, not as a sitting one
stops.campa: A hundred years after the hill at Kaniv, a bronze Shevchenko is unveiled off Dupont Circle before a crowd of about a hundred thousand, most of them the children and grandchildren of people who left the Russian and Austrian empires. Dwight Eisenhower, out of office three years, pulls the cord. The Soviet embassy objects. The statue of a serf who wrote in a forbidden language is placed in the capital of a republic during a cold war, which is the third distinct political use his name has been put to and not the last.
suggested_refs: The Taras Shevchenko Memorial, 2200 block of P Street NW, Washington, dedicated 27 June 1964

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the hornero in the bronze arms
stops.date_confidence: the monument and the nest are attested in the corpus; the date is that of the corpus photograph, not of the monument's erection
stops.campa: In the Jardin de los Poetas in Palermo a bronze Shevchenko stands among the park's other poets, and a hornero has built its clay oven in the crook of the statue. The park administration removes the nest. The bird rebuilds it within days. Ral Veroni's Platense symbology takes that oven-house, capped with a red Phrygian cap, as its emblem, and this is the famous one. Borges grew up a few streets away, Charly Garcia a few more, and Tschiffely rode out for Washington from the Sociedad Rural down the avenue.
suggested_refs: The Shevchenko monument in the Jardin de los Poetas, Parque 3 de Febrero, Palermo
Ral Veroni's hornero emblem in the Platense symbology
